Body HTML:
Hot water boilers for residential and light commercial hydronic heating, from 38,000 to 399,000 BTU/h input. The collection holds three types. Condensing boilers, such as the Navien NHB-H and NFB-H, IBC SL and VX, US Boiler Alta and Aspen and Lochinvar KHB, WHB and Noble, vent through plastic or stainless pipe; the IBC and US Boiler models are listed at 95 to 96 percent efficiency. Cast iron boilers, the US Boiler (Burnham) Series 2e chimney vented and X-PV power vented models, are listed at 84 to 85 percent and suit older high-temperature radiator systems. Combi boilers, such as the Navien NCB-H and NFC-H and the IBC CX and SFC, add domestic hot water on demand to space heating.

A condensing boiler reaches its rated efficiency only when the return water is cool enough to condense the flue gas, so the emitters and controls matter as much as the boiler.

How to choose

  • BTU input: size the boiler from a heat-loss calculation for the building, not from the rating plate of the old boiler.
  • Boiler type and return temperature: a condensing boiler needs low return water temperature, which means radiant floor, panel radiators sized for lower water temperature or an outdoor reset control. A cast iron boiler tolerates high return temperature and needs a bypass or mixing arrangement to protect it against thermal shock.
  • Fuel: Navien boilers are listed as natural gas and propane convertible. For other brands, check the gas type in the product title.
  • Venting: Series 2e boilers are chimney vented and X-PV boilers are power vented. Condensing boilers need PVC, polypropylene or stainless venting plus a neutralized condensate drain.
  • Circulator and elevation: product titles state "Includes Grundfos Pump" or "No Pump Included" and give the elevation range, such as 0-2,000 ft or 0-10,000 ft.

Common questions

Condensing or cast iron boiler?

A condensing boiler reaches its rated efficiency only with low return water temperature, such as radiant floor or an outdoor reset control. A cast iron boiler tolerates high return temperature and suits older high-temperature radiator systems.

Does the boiler include a circulator pump?

Check the product title. Many listings say Includes Grundfos Pump or No Pump Included. If no pump is included, add one from circulator pumps.

What size boiler do I need?

Size the boiler from a heat-loss calculation for the building, not from the rating of the old boiler. Older boilers were often oversized. For a combi, also check the hot water side: a combi that heats the house can still be short for two showers at once.

Shop by type or brand: condensing boilers, combi boilers, cast iron gas boilers, Navien boilers and Burnham boilers.

Body HTML:
A condensing boiler recovers extra heat by cooling the flue gas until its water vapor condenses. The collection includes Navien NHB and NHB-H wall-hung boilers from 55,000 to 150,000 BTU/h and NFB models from 175,000 to 399,000 BTU/h, IBC SL G3 fire tube boilers from 85,000 to 260,000 BTU/h and the IBC VX series, US Boiler (Burnham) Alta water tube and Aspen fire tube boilers, and Lochinvar KHB, WHB and Noble boilers. The IBC and US Boiler models are listed at 95 to 96 percent efficiency, with elevation ranges up to 10,000 or 12,000 feet depending on the model.

These boilers reach their rated efficiency only with low return water temperatures, so review the emitters and the controls before choosing one.

How to choose

  • BTU input and turndown: size the boiler to a room-by-room heat-loss calculation, and check the turndown ratio so it modulates well at low loads. Navien NHB-H titles list up to 15:1 turndown.
  • Return water temperature: radiant floors, low-temperature emitters and outdoor reset controls keep the return water cool enough for the boiler to condense.
  • Venting: confirm the vent material and the maximum vent length for the model. Sealed-combustion condensing boilers vent in PVC, CPVC, polypropylene or stainless, as the manufacturer lists.
  • Fuel and elevation: Navien models are listed as natural gas and propane convertible. Check the gas type, the gas supply size and the elevation range in the title.
  • Pump and condensate: Alta titles list an included Grundfos pump, while Aspen, SL and VX titles list no pump. Plan a condensate drain and a neutralizer.

Common questions

Why does a condensing boiler need low return water temperature?

It only condenses flue gas, and reaches its rated efficiency, when return water is cool enough. Radiant floors, low-temperature emitters and outdoor reset controls help.

Does a condensing boiler need a condensate neutralizer?

The condensate is acidic, so most installations need a drain and a neutralizer. See condensate neutralizers.

What venting does a condensing boiler use?

Sealed-combustion condensing boilers vent in PVC, CPVC, polypropylene or stainless, as the manufacturer lists. Check the maximum vent length for your model.

Related collections: all boilers, combi boilers, Navien boilers, condensate neutralizers and polypropylene vent pipe.

Body HTML:
A combi boiler provides space heating and domestic hot water on demand from one unit, so there is no separate water heater or indirect tank. The collection includes IBC CX combi boilers at 150,000 and 199,000 BTU/h with 10:1 turndown, IBC SFC combi boilers from 125,000 to 199,000 BTU/h listed at 94 to 95 percent efficiency, and Navien NCB-H and NFC-H condensing combi boilers with 60,000 to 199,900 BTU/h of heating input and up to 210,000 BTU/h for hot water. The US Boiler (Burnham) Alta ALTAC-200 is listed here as well.

Domestic hot water demand usually sets the input of a combi, so a model that heats the house well can still be short for two showers running at once. Check both sides before ordering.

How to choose

  • Heating input: it must cover the calculated heat loss of the building. Check the minimum firing rate if the system has small zones.
  • Hot water input: the domestic side has to keep up with the fixtures that run at the same time. Navien titles list both figures, for example 110,000 BTU/h heating and 199,900 BTU/h hot water on the NCB-240/110H.
  • Fuel and gas line: Navien NFC-H models and the NCB-240/110H are listed as natural gas and propane convertible. Size the gas line for the full input.
  • Venting and condensate: confirm the venting options for the model and plan a condensate drain.
  • System pump: the IBC SFC160-1 title lists a built-in pump; the SFC125 and SFC199 titles list no pump included.

Common questions

How do I size a combi boiler?

Check two numbers: the heating input must cover the heat loss, and the hot water side must keep up with the fixtures that run at the same time. Hot water demand usually sets the input.

Combi boiler or boiler with an indirect tank?

A combi saves space because there is no tank. A boiler with an indirect water heater stores hot water and handles several fixtures at once more easily.

Is a system pump included?

It depends on the model. Check the product title and specifications before ordering.

Related collections: Navien combi boilers, condensing boilers, indirect water heaters, IBC boilers and parts and condensate neutralizers.

Body HTML:
A Navien combi boiler heats the home and makes domestic hot water on demand from one wall-hung condensing unit, so there is no separate water heater or indirect tank. Two series are listed here. The NCB-H pairs 60,000 to 150,000 BTU/h of heating input with 160,000 or 199,900 BTU/h for hot water: the NCB-190/060H, NCB-190/080H, NCB-240/110H, NCB-240/130H and NCB-250/150H. The larger NFC-H fire-tube combi, the NFC-250/175H and NFC-250/200H, offers 175,000 or 199,900 BTU/h of heating with 210,000 BTU/h for hot water.

All are indoor wall-hung models. The first number in a Navien combi model name refers to the hot water side and the second to the heating side, so read both before comparing two models.

How to choose

  • Heating input: it should cover the calculated heat loss of the building. The NCB-H runs from 60,000 to 150,000 BTU/h and the NFC-H is 175,000 or 199,900 BTU/h.
  • Hot water input: the hot water side has to keep up with the fixtures that run at the same time, so check the hot water flow at your temperature rise. Inputs are 160,000 BTU/h on the NCB-190, 199,900 BTU/h on the NCB-240 and NCB-250, and 210,000 BTU/h on the NFC-250.
  • Fuel: the NCB-240/110H and both NFC-H models are listed as natural gas and propane convertible. Size the gas line for the full input.
  • Venting and condensate: plan for PVC, CPVC or polypropylene venting and a condensate drain with a neutralizer.
  • Side-by-side specs: compare every model in the Navien model comparison.

Common questions

What is the difference between the NCB-240/110H and the NCB-240/130H?

Both have 199,900 BTU/h of input for hot water. The NCB-240/110H has 110,000 BTU/h of heating input and the NCB-240/130H has 130,000 BTU/h.

NCB-H or NFC-H?

The NCB-H covers heating inputs up to 150,000 BTU/h. The NFC-H is the larger fire-tube combi, with 175,000 or 199,900 BTU/h of heating input and 210,000 BTU/h for hot water.

Can a Navien combi replace my boiler and water heater?

Yes. A combi heats the home and makes domestic hot water on demand from one wall-hung unit. Size it for both the heat loss and the fixtures that run at the same time.

Body HTML:
When a boiler stops heating, short-cycles or leaks, the fix is usually one part, not a new boiler. This collection brings together replacement parts for hot water and steam boilers, listed by manufacturer part number so you can match the number on the old part or in the boiler parts list.

Controls and ignition: aquastats and immersion wells (Resideo L8148, L4006, L4008, L6006), gas valves, hot surface igniters, ignition modules, pilot burners, thermocouples and low water cut-offs. Water side: pressure relief valves, fill and feed valves, expansion tanks, air eliminators, air vents, boiler drains, gauges and boiler trim kits. The collection also holds Taco and Grundfos circulators and US Boiler (Burnham) factory parts.

How to choose

  • Part number: match the number on the old part or in the boiler parts list. Check the boiler model and serial number on the rating plate first.
  • Voltage: controls are listed as 24 V, 120 V or millivolt. Match the control circuit of the boiler.
  • Connection size: compare the thread or sweat size of the old part, such as 1/2" or 3/4" NPT on immersion wells and 3/4" on boiler relief valves.
  • Relief valve rating: match the set pressure marked on the old valve and on the boiler rating plate. The Watts 3/4" iron boiler relief valve here is listed at 30 psi.
  • Brand parts: US Boiler kits are matched to a series, an input size or a section count, so read the full title.

Common questions

How do I find the right boiler part?

Start with the boiler model and serial number on the rating plate, then match the part number on the old part, its voltage and its connection size. Our zone valve replacement guide and the Zone Planner can help with zoning parts.

Can I replace a gas valve or ignition control myself?

Gas valve, ignition and burner work should be done by a qualified heating technician.

Which parts control boiler pressure?

The fill valve keeps the system at its cold-fill pressure, the expansion tank takes up the water volume as it heats, and the relief valve opens if pressure reaches its set point.

Go straight to aquastats and wells, boiler fill valves, circulator pumps, zone valves or US Boiler / Burnham parts.

Navien parts and accessories for NPE tankless water heaters, NCB and NFC combi boilers and NHB and NFB boilers. Complete units are not included here. The range covers concentric vent terminations, elbows, extensions, wall flanges and roof flashing, series parts kits for NPE, NPE-2, NCB, NFB-H and NFC-H units, Ready-Link racks, NHB and NFB primary manifolds, NaviLink Wi-Fi control, temperature sensors, cascade cables, SmartZone+ switching relays, the NaviClean magnetic filter and PeakFlow anti-scale systems.

Most of these parts are model-specific, and some are specific to a serial range. Navien revises components without changing the appliance name, so order from the data plate, not from the model family. A vent kit for an NPE is not an NCB kit.

How to choose

  • Model and serial number: read both from the data plate of the appliance before ordering.
  • Vent diameter: wall flange and vent terminator kits are listed in 2" and 3", and concentric elbows in 80-125 mm. Match the vent system already installed.
  • Termination type: sidewall termination kits are listed in 11.5" and 21", and the concentric roof termination in 13" with adjustable roof flashing. Terminations have code and manufacturer clearances from windows, doors, soffits and property lines.
  • Series parts kit: pick the kit named for your series: NPE, NPE-2, NCB and NCB-E, NFB-H, NFC-H or NR/NP.
  • Racks and manifolds: the Ready-Link Rack (V4) base and add-on are listed for NPE, NCB, NFB and NHB units; primary manifolds are separate for NHB and NFB.

Common questions

How do I find the right Navien part?

Order from the data plate, using the full model and serial number. Navien revises components without changing the appliance name, and some parts are specific to a serial range.

Will an NPE vent kit fit an NCB combi boiler?

No. Vent kits are model-specific, and a vent kit for an NPE is not an NCB kit. Check the kit title against your model.

Can I reuse the old gasket in a concentric vent joint?

Reusing an old gasket in a concentric joint is a common source of condensate leaks. A concentric vent carries intake and exhaust in one pipe, so a damaged termination or cracked flange takes the unit out of service.

For complete units, see all Navien products, Navien combi boilers, Navien boilers and Navien tankless water heaters. Parts for other tankless brands are in tankless repair parts.

Replacement parts and kits for US Boiler (Burnham) boilers, listed by factory part number. U.S. Boiler Company makes the Burnham residential boilers, so Burnham part numbers are supported here. The collection includes gas valves, Ebm-Papst blowers, ignitors and flame sensors, fuse sets, temperature sensors and service kits for Alta, Phantom II and K2WT condensing boilers; Alpine ignitor and flame sensor gasket sets; natural gas to propane conversion kits by section count; direct vent conversion kits for X-PV; IQ low water cut-off and outdoor reset kits; and flexible double-wall oil vent and a Beckett AFG air intake and vent kit for oil boilers.

Kits are matched to a specific series, input size or section count, so confirm the boiler model, section count and serial number on the rating plate before ordering.

How to choose

  • Series and model: titles name the boilers each part fits, such as Alta, Alpine, Aspen, K2WT, Phantom II, X-PV and MPO-IQ.
  • Input size: condensing boiler parts are split by input in MBH, for example blowers for 080-136 MBH and for 150-200 MBH.
  • Section count: gas conversion kits are listed for 2, 3-6 and 7-9 section boilers, and direct vent conversion kits for 3 to 8 sections.
  • Altitude: the natural gas to propane conversion kits are listed for 0-2,000 ft. Check the altitude limit before ordering.
  • Gas valve size: electronic ignition gas valves are listed in 1/2" x 1/2" and 3/4" x 3/4".

Common questions

How do I find the right US Boiler part?

Use the boiler model, section count and serial number from the rating plate. Kits are matched to specific series such as Alta, Alpine, MPO-IQ, Series 2e and X-PV.

Are Burnham and US Boiler parts the same?

Yes. U.S. Boiler Company makes the Burnham residential boilers, so Burnham part numbers are supported under US Boiler.

Can I replace a gas valve or safety control myself?

Gas valves, limits and venting changes should be replaced by a qualified technician and checked with a combustion test after installation.

Related collections: all US Boiler products, Burnham boilers, cast iron gas boilers, boiler parts and low water cut-offs.

Body HTML:
An indirect water heater makes domestic hot water using heat from a boiler. Hot boiler water circulates through a coil inside the tank and heats the potable water around it, so the tank has no burner or flue of its own. The collection includes IBC indirect tanks in 444 stainless steel with an aquastat, from 26.8 to 119 gallons, including the DTI-40, DTI-55, DTI-65, DTI-80 and DTI-80MAX; AquaFlow stainless steel indirect-fired water heaters from 30 to 119 gallons (AF-30 through AF-119); Heat-Flo 30 and 40 gallon indirect tanks with top connections and a 60 gallon high-output model with an element; and Lochinvar stainless steel single-wall hot water makers.

Because the tank stores hot water, it handles several fixtures running at once more easily than an on-demand combi.

How to choose

  • Tank capacity: size the tank to the peak hot water demand of the household. Sizes here run from 26.8 to 119 gallons.
  • Boiler output: check the boiler output available for the hot water zone and the first hour rating of the tank at your boiler supply temperature.
  • Coil connections: confirm the connection size and position. The IBC DTI-80MAX and the 119 gallon IBC tank list 1-1/2" inlets, and Heat-Flo tanks list top connections.
  • Control and piping: IBC tanks come with an aquastat. Decide whether the tank will be piped as a priority zone.
  • Safety valves: install a T&P relief valve, and a thermostatic mixing valve where required.

Common questions

How does an indirect water heater work?

Hot water from the boiler runs through a coil inside the tank and heats the potable water around it. The tank has no burner or flue of its own.

What size indirect water heater do I need?

Size it to peak hot water demand and to the boiler output available for the hot water zone. Check the first hour rating and the coil connections.

Does an indirect tank need an anode rod?

Stainless steel tanks such as AquaFlow need no sacrificial anode. Check the product details for other brands.

Related collections: boilers, condensing boilers, Heat-Flo, mixing valves and water heater T&P relief valves.

Body HTML:
A circulator moves water around a closed loop instead of lifting it from a source, so it is sized for flow and head loss through the piping, not for pressure. The collection includes Taco 00 series circulators such as the 007, 0010 and 0015, Taco ECM models such as the 007e, 0015e3 and 0018e, Grundfos UPS15-58FC, UPS26-99, ALPHA and MAGNA circulators, Grundfos UP15 bronze pumps and Resideo ECM and 3-speed circulators.

Fixed-speed circulators run on one curve and are matched to the loop at installation. Variable-speed ECM circulators adjust their own speed, which matters most on systems with zone valves, where the flow demand changes as zones open and close. An oversized pump shows up as noise and short-cycling, and an undersized one leaves cold zones at the end of the run.

How to choose

  • Flow and head: work out the flow in GPM and the head loss in feet for the loop, then compare them with the pump curve. Some titles list the maximum figures, such as 19 ft of head and 18 gpm on the Grundfos UPS15-58FC.
  • Body material: cast iron bodies are for closed hydronic loops only, because the oxygen in fresh water corrodes them. Open loops and potable water, such as domestic hot water recirculation, need a stainless steel or bronze body.
  • Connection: pumps are listed as flanged, union or sweat. Match the flange spacing and size of the pump being replaced.
  • Voltage: most models here are listed at 115 V; Grundfos MAGNA models are listed at 115-230 V.
  • Speed and options: choose fixed speed, 3-speed, ECM variable speed or Delta-T control, with or without an integral flow check (IFC).

Common questions

How do I size a circulator pump?

Size the pump from the flow and head loss of the loop, not from pressure. An oversized pump is noisy and an undersized one leaves cold zones.

Cast iron, bronze or stainless steel?

Use cast iron on closed hydronic heating loops. Use bronze or stainless steel for potable water and hot water recirculation.

What do I need to match when replacing a circulator?

Most residential circulators use the standard flange bolt pattern, so replacing one is usually a matter of matching the flange spacing and the electrical supply. Check the flow and head of the old pump as well.

Shop by type or brand: Taco circulator pumps, Grundfos, variable speed circulators, hot water recirculating pumps and pump flanges and accessories.

Body HTML:
Zone valves, replacement heads and parts for hydronic heating, plus dampers and panels for forced-air zoning. The collection includes Honeywell V8043 and V4043 2-way and V8044 and V4044 3-way zone valves, VC series valves, actuators and cartridges, VU fan coil valves, Taco Zone Sentry, QuickTop and heat motor valves, Caleffi and Viega products, Honeywell TrueZONE panels and zone dampers. Connections are sweat, press, flare and NPT in 1/2" through 1". The V8043 and VC lines are now made by Resideo under the same numbers.

Most residential zone valves fail at the powerhead, not the valve body. Replacement heads swap without draining the system, which is the simpler fix when a zone stops responding but the valve still moves by hand.

Popular part numbers: Honeywell V8043A1011, Honeywell V8043E1137, Honeywell 40003916-021, Honeywell VCZZ1100, Honeywell VU842A1046.

How to choose

  • Voltage: V8043 and V8044 valves are listed at 24 Vac, and V4043 and V4044 valves at 120 Vac. Match the old valve and the zone control.
  • Size and connection: match the pipe size (1/2", 3/4" or 1") and the sweat, flare, NPT or press connection. Fan coil valves also list a Cv, such as 1.0 or 2.5 Cv on the VU52.
  • Valve action: choose 2-way or 3-way (diverting), and normally closed or normally open, to match the valve being replaced.
  • End switch: pick a valve or head with an end switch if the old one had one.
  • Circulator: as zones close, flow through the remaining ones rises, so a valve-zoned system usually wants a pressure bypass or a variable-speed circulator.

Common questions

Can I replace just the zone valve head?

Often, yes. If the valve body still opens and closes by hand, a replacement head fixes the zone without draining the system.

Normally open or normally closed?

A normally closed valve stays shut until the thermostat powers it open. A normally open valve stays open until it is powered closed. Match the old valve.

What does the end switch do?

The end switch closes when the valve is fully open and tells the boiler or circulator to run. Pick a valve with an end switch if the old one had one.

Shop by brand or part: Honeywell zone valves, Taco zone valves, replacement heads, switching relays and zone controls and variable speed circulators.

Body HTML:
An aquastat switches a burner or a circulator according to water temperature. This collection covers Resideo aquastat controls and immersion wells for boilers and water heaters: L8148 aquastat relays, L4006 immersion aquastats in 100 to 240 °F and 130 to 270 °F ranges, L4008 high limit controls with capillary, L6006 and L6008 high or low limit and circulator controllers, the L7224U universal electronic oil aquastat, copper immersion wells in 1/2" and 3/4" NPT with 3" insertion depth, and heat conductive grease. Resideo makes the Honeywell Home aquastat line under the same model numbers.

Popular part numbers: Resideo L8148E1299, Resideo L4006E1125, Resideo L4008E1156, Resideo L6006C1018, Resideo L7224U1002, Resideo 120650.

How to choose

  • Function: decide whether the control must break on rise as a high limit, make on fall as a low limit, or run a circulator. Check the switching action, SPST or SPDT.
  • Temperature range and differential: confirm the setpoint range covers the application, for example 100-240 °F with a 5-30 °F adjustable differential on the L4006A.
  • Reset: high limits are listed with automatic or manual reset. Match the old control.
  • Well: many controls are sold "less well". Match the well size and insertion depth to the tapping and the control bulb, and apply heat conductive grease for accurate sensing.
  • Voltage: check the control circuit; the L8148E1299 relay is listed for low voltage and millivolt systems.

Common questions

How do I choose a replacement aquastat?

Match the part number on the old control, such as L8148E1299 or L4006E1125. If that number is discontinued, match the function (high limit, low limit or circulator), the temperature range and whether it needs a well.

Can I reuse the existing immersion well?

Usually, if the new control has the same bulb size and insertion depth. Add heat conductive grease to the well so the sensor reads the water temperature correctly.

Is a Resideo aquastat the same as a Honeywell aquastat?

Yes. Resideo makes the Honeywell Home aquastat line under the same model numbers. See all Resideo controls.

Related collections: boiler parts, low water cut-offs, temperature and pressure gauges and controls, switches and sensors.

Body HTML:
A boiler fill valve, also called a boiler feed valve or pressure reducing valve, keeps a hydronic heating system at its cold-fill pressure, usually 12 to 15 psi for a typical two-story home. It adds make-up water automatically when the pressure drops. The collection lists fill and feed valves by part number: Caleffi AutoFill 553 series valves with or without a pressure gauge, Caleffi 573 and 574 COMBO models with a built-in backflow preventer, Resideo NK300S combination feed valves and the FM911 fill valve and backflow preventer assembly, and Taco 329 fast-fill and 335 boiler feed valves. The Caleffi F59650 replacement cartridge for the 553 series is listed as well.

If the boiler pressure keeps falling, the fill valve never shuts off or the relief valve drips, a worn or clogged fill valve is a common cause.

How to choose

  • Connection size and type: match the inlet and outlet, 1/2" or 3/4", in NPT, sweat, press or union.
  • Pressure setting: the valve must cover the cold-fill pressure of the system. Caleffi lists the AutoFill 553 as factory set at 15 psi and adjustable from 3 to 60 psi.
  • Backflow protection: many local codes require a backflow preventer on the boiler fill line. A combination valve saves space and two joints. Check whether your installation needs an ASSE 1012 or an ASSE 1013 device.
  • Pressure gauge: Caleffi 553642A and 553649A include a downstream gauge; other models are sold without one.

Common questions

What pressure should a boiler fill valve be set to?

The cold-fill pressure is usually 12 to 15 psi for a typical two-story home. Caleffi AutoFill 553 valves are factory set at 15 psi and adjust from 3 to 60 psi. Follow the boiler manufacturer instructions for your system.

Is a boiler fill valve the same as a boiler feed valve?

Yes. Fill valve, feed valve and pressure reducing valve are names for the same part on a hydronic heating system.

Do I need a backflow preventer on the fill line?

Many local codes require one. Combination models such as the Caleffi 573 COMBO and the Resideo FM911 put the fill valve and the backflow preventer in one assembly. See also backflow preventers.

Air eliminators, air separators and hydraulic separators for hydronic heating systems. An air eliminator takes air out of the system water so it can be vented, and a hydraulic separator decouples the boiler loop from the system loop. The collection includes Resideo SuperVent air eliminators in NPT, sweat and press connections from 3/4" to 1-1/2", SuperVent replacement vent tops, Webstone press brass air separators from 3/4" to 1-1/2", the Taco 4900 series air separator and Taco air scoops, Legend Valve air and debris eliminators, Caleffi DISCAL DIRTMAG air and dirt separators with magnet, Caleffi hydro separators with sweat and press unions, and the Caleffi DiscalAir high discharge automatic air vent.

Install the air separator where the water is hottest and the pressure lowest, usually on the boiler supply ahead of the pump.

How to choose

  • Pipe size and flow: size the separator by pipe size and flow rate. Some titles list a Cv, such as 22 Cv on the 1" press SuperVent PV100P.
  • Connection: match NPT, sweat, press or union connections to the piping.
  • Function: choose an air eliminator, a combined air and dirt separator, or a hydraulic separator, depending on what the system needs.
  • Orientation: check whether the unit is for horizontal or vertical pipe; Webstone lists a separate 1" vertical model (H-78004-V).
  • Service parts: replacement vent tops are listed for Resideo SuperVent and Webstone air separators.

Common questions

Where should an air eliminator be installed?

Where the water is hottest and the pressure lowest, usually on the boiler supply ahead of the pump.

What is the difference between an air separator and a hydraulic separator?

An air separator removes air from the system water. A hydraulic separator decouples the boiler loop from the system loop so the flow in one does not disturb the other.

Can the vent top be replaced?

Yes, on some models. The Resideo PV-001RP and PV-020RP are replacement vent tops for SuperVent, and the Webstone H-74000 is a replacement vent assembly for 3/4" to 2" air separators.

Hydronic expansion tanks and mounting hardware for closed-loop heating systems. The tank takes up the extra water volume as the system heats, which keeps the pressure below the relief valve setting. The collection includes Amtrol Extrol EX-15, EX-30 and EX-60 tanks, Zilmet ZHT tanks from 2.1 to 6.3 gallons and ZFT rectangular tanks, and Calefactio HGT tanks from 2.1 to 8 gallons, along with the Flamco 1/2" wall mount bracket and Axiom HN-2 and HN-3 wall bracket kits. The Axiom HN-3 Hydro-NODE comes with a 3-way expansion tank service valve, two 1/2" ball valves, a manual air vent and a pressure gauge; the tank is not part of that kit.

Heating tanks are not designed for potable water, so use a potable-rated thermal expansion tank on domestic water heaters.

How to choose

  • Tank volume: size the tank from the system water volume, the fill pressure, and the maximum operating temperature and pressure. Tanks here run from 2 to 8 gallons.
  • Precharge: set the tank precharge to match the system fill pressure before installing. Amtrol lists a 12 psig factory precharge on Extrol EX tanks.
  • Ratings: check the maximum working pressure and temperature of the tank against the system. Amtrol lists the Extrol EX at 100 psig and 240 °F.
  • Mounting: decide between hanging the tank from the piping and a wall bracket, and check the connection size in the product details.

Common questions

What size expansion tank do I need for my boiler?

Size it from the system water volume, the fill pressure and the maximum operating temperature and pressure. Manufacturer sizing tables use these inputs.

What should the precharge pressure be?

Set the precharge to match the system fill pressure before the tank is installed. Amtrol Extrol EX tanks are listed with a 12 psig factory precharge.

Can I use a heating expansion tank on a water heater?

No. Heating tanks are not designed for potable water. Use a tank from expansion tanks for water heating.

Manifolds and accessories for radiant floor heating. A manifold feeds supply water to each PEX loop and collects the return, and flow meters or balancing valves on the manifold let you set each loop. The collection includes MrPEX Systems 1-1/4" stainless steel manifold assemblies with flow meters and ball valves in up to 12 branches, MrPEX 1-1/2" chrome plated brass manifolds and composite manifold kits, Viega stainless steel heating and cooling manifolds, HeatLink 1-1/4" stainless steel manifolds with flow meters and PEX manifold tees, EK 20 and EK 25 loop adapters for 5/16" through 3/4" PEX, end caps, valve actuators, manifold cabinets and Caleffi manifold housing boxes.

Pressure test the loops before the floor is poured.

How to choose

  • Loop count: size the manifold by the number of loops. Assemblies here are listed with up to 12 branches.
  • Balancing: use models with flow meters or balancing valves where the loops differ in length.
  • Manifold and connection size: check the trunk size (1-1/4" or 1-1/2") and the supply and return connections, such as 1-1/4" x 1" union x FPT on Viega manifolds.
  • Loop adapters: match the EK 20 or EK 25 fitting assembly to the PEX size and type.
  • Actuators: actuators are listed as 2-wire or 4-wire. Confirm the actuator voltage against your zoning controls.

Common questions

How many loops can one manifold serve?

One loop per branch. Count the loops in the zone and pick a manifold with at least that many branches; assemblies here are listed with up to 12.

Do I need flow meters on a radiant manifold?

Use a manifold with flow meters or balancing valves where the loops differ in length, so each loop can be set.

What are EK 20 and EK 25 adapters?

They are the MrPEX fitting assemblies that connect PEX to a manifold branch, listed for sizes such as 3/4" PEX to EK 20 and 5/8" PEX to EK 25. Match the adapter to the manifold outlet and to the PEX size and type.

Taco Comfort Solutions circulators, zone valves and hydronic system parts. Pumps include 00 series cast iron circulators such as the 007 and the 0010 through 0015, with integral flow check options, ECM variable speed models such as the 007e, 0015e3, 0018e, 0026e and 0034e, stainless steel 006, 007, 008 and 009 circulators and Plumb N' Plug pumps with timers. Zoning parts include Zone Sentry, QuickTop and heat motor zone valves, SR500 series switching relays, ZVC400 series zone valve controls and the X-Pump Block. The collection also holds Hy-Vent air vents, the 4900 series air separator, 5000 series mixing valves, ACCU-FLO balancing valves, Freedom flange sets, replacement cartridges and 329 and 335 boiler feed valves.

Planning a zoned system? Try the Zone Planner.

How to choose

  • Flow and head: size a circulator to the flow and head the loop requires and compare them with the pump curve.
  • Body material: cast iron circulators suit closed heating loops. Use bronze or stainless steel bodies for open potable water systems.
  • Connections and voltage: confirm flanged, union or sweat connections and the supply voltage; most circulators here are listed at 115V/60/1.
  • Zone valves: match the pipe size, the sweat or press connection, normally closed or normally open action and the control voltage to your system.
  • Relays and controls: pick by the number of zones. SR switching relays are listed from 1 to 6 zones, with priority on multi-zone models.

Common questions

Taco 007 or 007e?

The 007 is the fixed-speed circulator, listed here in cast iron and stainless steel. The 007e is listed as a cast iron ECM high efficiency model. Compare the pump curves before swapping one for the other.

Switching relay or zone valve control?

SR500 series switching relays are listed for zoning with circulators, and ZVC400 series controls for zoning with zone valves. Pick the one that matches how the system is zoned.

Can I replace only the cartridge in a Taco circulator?

Replacement cartridges are listed in Taco cartridges. Match the cartridge to the pump model.

IBC boilers, indirect water heaters and service parts. The boilers are gas condensing models: SL G3 fire tube boilers from 85,000 to 260,000 BTU/h (SL 10-85, SL 14-115, SL 20-160, SL 30-199 and SL 26-260), VX series boilers at 110,000, 150,000 and 199,000 BTU/h, CX combi boilers at 150,000 and 199,000 BTU/h with 10:1 turndown, and SFC combi boilers from 125,000 to 199,000 BTU/h. Product titles list 94 to 96 percent efficiency and elevation ranges up to 10,000 or 12,000 feet. The collection also includes 444 stainless steel indirect water heaters from 26.8 to 119 gallons with aquastat, the SFT-199 tankless water heater, and replacement parts such as ignitor kits, fan kits, gas valve kits, sensors, control boards and parts kits.

For service parts, confirm the boiler model and series named in the part title.

How to choose

  • BTU input: size the boiler to a heat-loss calculation. Inputs here run from 85,000 to 260,000 BTU/h.
  • Heating only or combi: for CX and SFC combi units, check the domestic hot water flow as well as the heating output.
  • Pump: SL and VX titles list no pump included, and the SFC160-1 lists a built-in pump.
  • Elevation and fuel: SL titles list 0-12,000 ft and VX and SFC titles 0-10,000 ft. Check the gas type in the title before ordering.
  • Indirect tank: match the tank to the boiler output and to household hot water demand.

Common questions

IBC SL or VX series?

Both are fire tube condensing boilers listed at 95 to 96 percent efficiency. The SL G3 runs from 85,000 to 260,000 BTU/h with a listed elevation range up to 12,000 ft; the VX runs from 110,000 to 199,000 BTU/h with a range up to 10,000 ft. Compare the specifications of the two sizes you are considering.

Does an IBC boiler include a circulator?

It depends on the model. Titles state No Pump Included or Built-In Pump. If none is included, see circulator pumps.

How do I find the right IBC part?

Part titles name the series they fit, such as SL G1/G2/G3, VX, HC/DC or SFT and SFC. Confirm the boiler model and series before ordering.

Grundfos circulator pumps and pump connection parts. The collection includes UPS15-58FC and UPSe ECM cast iron circulators for closed heating loops, UPS15-55SFC and UPS26-99SFC stainless steel models, ALPHA and ALPHA2 variable speed ECM circulators, MAGNA1 and MAGNA3 circulators with listed heads up to 59 ft and flows up to 85 gpm, UP15-18 bronze circulators with 1/2" and 3/4" sweat connections, the UP15-10SU7P Comfort and ALPHA HWR hot water recirculation pumps and the Comfort valve. Connection parts include cast iron and bronze pump flange sets from 3/4" to 1-1/2", union sets, clip-on aquastat kits and timer kits.

Use cast iron bodies on closed hydronic loops, and bronze or stainless steel for potable water and recirculation.

How to choose

  • Flow and head: size the pump by the required flow and head. Titles list maximum figures on several models, such as 19 ft and 18 gpm on the UPS15-58FC and 33 ft and 42 gpm on the UPSe 26-99F.
  • Body material: cast iron for closed heating loops; bronze or stainless steel for potable water.
  • Connection: pumps are listed as flanged, union or sweat. Match the flange or union set to the pump model and the pipe size.
  • Voltage: most models are listed at 115 V; MAGNA models are listed at 115 V or 115-230 V.
  • Recirculation control: recirculation pumps are listed with a timer and line cord, and clip-on aquastat kits are sold separately for UP series pumps.

Common questions

Cast iron or stainless steel Grundfos circulator?

Use cast iron on closed hydronic heating loops. Use bronze or stainless steel for potable water and hot water recirculation, such as the UPS26-99SFC.

How do I pick the right flanges for a Grundfos pump?

Match the flange or union set to the pump model and the pipe size. See pump flanges.

How do I size a circulator?

Size the pump from the flow and head loss of the loop, not from pressure. An oversized pump is noisy and an undersized one leaves cold zones. See all circulator pumps.
